A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AHOY research and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. All supplied pages were checked. Neither PDF contains an appendix; both refer to supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and animation experiments on YouTube videos and BEHAVE, including quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–2 and component ablations in Table 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, quantitative comparisons and ablations in Section 4 and Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same coarse avatar construction, Wan 2.2 finetuning, RF-Inversion supervision, pose-dependent Gaussian maps, map/LBS pose decoupling, FLAME head supervision and inference procedure. No algorithmic component or loss changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use YouTube videos and BEHAVE for the same reconstruction, animation, novel-view and novel-pose tasks. Difficult-pose examples and animation within reconstructed 3D scenes are also retained; no dataset or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains PSHuman, SyncHuman, LHM and IDOL; Table 2 retains LHM and IDOL. The newly cited RAGA work is discussed as related research, without becoming an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain 50 YouTube videos, 8 BEHAVE sequences, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, occluded versus generated canonical inputs, held-out YouTube frames, and BEHAVE side-camera and unseen-pose evaluation. No experimental setting or protocol is revised.

E4.justification: Section 4.5, Table 3 and Figure 7 retain the same four ablations: coarse avatar only, without RF-Inversion, without map/LBS decoupling, and without head/body split. The difficult-pose analysis in Figure 5 is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. No uncertainty reporting is introduced.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative findings in Figures 3–8 are retained. For example, AHOY's BEHAVE novel-view and novel-pose PSNR remain 24.12 and 22.81, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the accompanying Gaussian, pose, flow and supervision definitions are unchanged beyond formatting. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning reconstruction under heavy occlusion, hallucinated supervision, pose-dependent avatars, identity preservation and scene animation. The state-of-the-art performance claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of diffusion inconsistencies and component benefits remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning incorrect hallucinated details, dependence on diffusion fidelity and slow multistage optimization; added related-work prose reiterates existing design motivations.

D1.justification: The disclosed implementation procedures, model components, symbolic loss weights and project-page information are unchanged. Expanded funding and assistance acknowledgements provide no additional implementation settings or code/data access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds RAGA as an avatar-scene composition reference and briefly expands the positioning of explicit 3DGS and diffusion-generated supervision. The other 156 bibliography entries match after renumbering, making this a limited contextual addition.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammar and punctuation edits, expands related-work explanations, updates affiliations, adds an equal-advising note and expands acknowledgements. The section sequence and technical narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The same eight figures and three tables retain their content and structure. The affiliation block expands, links gain color, and floats reflow; for example, Figure 3 moves from before Section 3.3.4 to before Section 4.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides clearer contextual explanations in Section 2 linking 3DGS composition and hallucinated supervision to the task, supported by a relevant added citation. Together with small prose corrections, this modestly improves exposition and positioning. The scientific methods, evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
